trial_court: III Additional District Judge at Karimnagar, O.P.No.414 of 2007
case_name: Mylarapu Sarojana vs Mylarapu Mallamma And 4 Ors
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed application under Section 372 of Indian Succession Act for issuance of succession certificate and payment of death benefits to her husband's tune of Rs.3,09,371/-.

legal_principles.principle: A customary divorce must be signed by both spouses.
legal_principles.held: The learned III Additional District Judge at Karimnagar in the impugned order at page No.10 and paragraph No.17 has clearly stated that even according to the customs prevailing in the community, a customary divorce must be signed by both the spouses but in Ex.B1 there is no signature of deceased.

legal_principles.principle: The thumb impression of an illiterate person must be subscribed on a document.
legal_principles.held: But surprisingly, in Ex.B1 the name of the petitioner was written as if she is a literate. Further, a mere name as 'Mallamma' was written and her surname was also not mentioned.

outcome.final_order: The impugned order was set aside and the succession certificate granted in favour of respondent No.1 was revoked.
